mcq.q: What effect does friction have on rubbing your hands?
mcq.explanation: Friction produces heat.

mcq.q: What does a force do when it squeezes a sponge?
mcq.explanation: Squeezing changes the shape.

mcq.q: What effect of force is shown when a goalkeeper stops a ball?
mcq.explanation: The force of the hands stops the ball.

mcq.q: What effect is shown when a force starts a still football moving?
mcq.explanation: A push makes a still object move.

mcq.q: A cyclist pedals harder and goes faster. What effect of force is this?
mcq.explanation: More force increases speed.

mcq.q: A cyclist presses the brakes and slows down. What effect of force is this?
mcq.explanation: Brakes use friction to slow the bicycle.

mcq.q: A hockey stick hits a rolling ball to the left. What effect of force is this?
mcq.explanation: The direction of the ball changes.

mcq.q: Which of these holds objects together?
mcq.explanation: Glue, nails and ropes use forces to hold things together.

mcq.q: Why do we put oil on machine parts?
mcq.explanation: Oil makes surfaces slide easily.

mcq.q: Which of these reduces friction?
mcq.explanation: Ball bearings roll and reduce friction.

mcq.q: Where are ball bearings found?
mcq.explanation: Bicycle wheels use ball bearings.

mcq.q: Logs placed under a heavy load help it move because they act as
mcq.explanation: Rollers reduce friction.

mcq.q: Which of these is a way of increasing useful friction?
options: Wearing smooth socks on a wet floor
mcq.explanation: Rough soles grip the ground.

mcq.q: Why are tyres made with rough patterns?
mcq.explanation: Grip needs friction.

mcq.q: Why do matches light when rubbed on the box?
mcq.explanation: Rubbing produces heat.

mcq.q: Which is a use of gravity?
options: Lifting up a stone by itself
mcq.explanation: Gravity makes water flow downhill.

mcq.q: A stone and a crumpled paper are dropped together. They land almost together because
options: Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper
mcq.explanation: The air has very little effect on the crumpled paper.

mcq.q: A flat sheet of paper falls slower than a stone because
options: Air pushes up on the flat paper more
mcq.explanation: Air pushes up more on the wide flat sheet.

mcq.q: What is weight?
options: The pull of gravity on an object
mcq.explanation: Weight is the pull of gravity on a thing.

mcq.q: Which of these is a problem caused by friction?
options: Wearing away of shoes and tyres
mcq.explanation: Friction wears surfaces away.

mcq.q: Which of these is a use of friction?
mcq.explanation: Brakes use friction to slow wheels.

mcq.q: A wheelbarrow is easier to move than dragging a load because
mcq.explanation: Wheels roll and reduce friction.

mcq.q: Which force acts on a ball thrown into the air and brings it back down?
mcq.explanation: Gravity pulls the ball to the ground.

mcq.q: How can a farmer keep a wheelbarrow running smoothly?
mcq.explanation: Oil reduces friction.

mcq.q: Which of these needs friction to work?
mcq.explanation: Walking needs grip from friction.

mcq.q: What happens if there is no friction between your shoes and the ground?
mcq.explanation: Without friction you cannot grip.

mcq.q: Which of these can change the shape of dough?
mcq.explanation: A force can squeeze and stretch dough.

mcq.q: A force can be small or big. A bigger push makes a ball go
mcq.explanation: A stronger force has a bigger effect.

mcq.q: What happens when you push a book gently with a finger compared with a hard push?
options: It moves faster with the gentle push
It flies away with the gentle push
It moves slowly with the gentle push
It does not move with the hard push
mcq.explanation: A bigger force gives a bigger effect.

mcq.q: Which of these shows that friction produces heat?
mcq.explanation: Rubbing surfaces produces heat.

mcq.q: Which of these will make a block slide the shortest distance on a ramp?
mcq.explanation: Rough surfaces have the most friction.

mcq.q: What should you do when doing force experiments?
options: Keep fingers away from moving parts
mcq.explanation: Safe practice prevents injuries.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT an effect of force?
mcq.explanation: Colour is not caused by a force.

mcq.q: Pulling a rope in tug of war uses
mcq.explanation: Pulling is a force.

mcq.q: What direction does friction act in compared with the motion of an object?
mcq.explanation: Friction acts against motion.

mcq.q: A rolling ball slowly comes to a stop on the ground mainly because of
mcq.explanation: Friction between the ball and the ground slows it.

mcq.q: Which of these is a way of reducing friction on a bicycle chain?
mcq.explanation: Oil helps parts slide.

mcq.q: A pump pushing air into a tyre is an example of
mcq.explanation: The pump pushes air by force.

mcq.q: Which force is at work when you pour water and it flows down a slope?
mcq.explanation: Gravity pulls water downhill.

mcq.q: Which force makes it hard to push a heavy box along a rough floor?
mcq.explanation: Rough floor gives large friction.

mcq.q: Why do people spread ash or sand on a slippery path?
mcq.explanation: Rough material improves grip.

mcq.q: A ball is rolling and you kick it in the direction it moves. What happens?
mcq.explanation: A force in the direction of movement increases speed.

mcq.q: Which of these holds a shirt together?
mcq.explanation: Stitches hold cloth pieces together.

mcq.q: What does light help us to do?
mcq.explanation: Light lets us see objects.

mcq.q: What is a source of light?
options: Something that gives out its own light
mcq.explanation: A source of light makes its own light.

mcq.q: Which of these is a natural source of light?
mcq.explanation: The sun is found in nature.

mcq.q: A flash of light in the sky during a storm is a natural source of light. What is it?
mcq.explanation: Lightning is a natural flash of light.

mcq.q: Which small living thing makes its own light and so is a natural source?
mcq.explanation: Fireflies make their own light.

mcq.q: Which of these is a natural source of light at night?
mcq.explanation: Stars give out their own light.

mcq.q: Which of these is an artificial source of light?
mcq.explanation: Bulbs are made by people.

mcq.q: Which battery-powered device gives artificial light?
mcq.explanation: A torch is made by people.

mcq.q: Which of these gives artificial light by burning paraffin?
mcq.explanation: A paraffin lamp is a made light source.

mcq.q: Which of these artificial sources charges its battery in the sun?
mcq.explanation: A solar lamp is made by people.

mcq.q: The moon shines brightly at night. Why is it still not a source of light?
options: It reflects light from the sun
mcq.explanation: The moon does not make its own light.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT a source of light?
mcq.explanation: A mirror only reflects light.

mcq.q: How does light travel?
mcq.explanation: Light travels in straight lines.

mcq.q: What happens to light when it hits an opaque object?
mcq.explanation: Opaque objects do not let light pass.

mcq.q: What is a transparent material?
options: A material that lets almost all light pass through
A material that blocks all light
A material that is always red
mcq.explanation: Transparent materials let us see clearly through them.

mcq.q: Which of these is transparent?
mcq.explanation: Clear glass lets light through.

mcq.q: Which of these is translucent?
mcq.explanation: Tissue paper lets some light through.

mcq.q: Which of these is opaque?
mcq.explanation: Wood blocks light.

mcq.q: What does a translucent roof sheet do?
mcq.explanation: It lets daylight in but you cannot see through it clearly.

mcq.q: Why do houses have windows?
mcq.explanation: Windows allow sunlight to enter the room.

mcq.q: What is one benefit of using translucent roof sheets in a house?
options: It saves electricity in the day
mcq.explanation: Daylight comes in so lamps are not needed.

mcq.q: Which wall colour helps a room to be brighter?
mcq.explanation: Light colours reflect more light.

mcq.q: Which of these is an artificial way of lighting a house?
mcq.explanation: Bulbs are artificial light.

mcq.q: Which artificial light uses energy from the sun?
mcq.explanation: A solar lamp charges by day.

mcq.q: Why should candles and paraffin lamps be kept away from curtains?
mcq.explanation: Flames can set cloth on fire.

mcq.q: Which of these is a safety use of light?
mcq.explanation: Street lights help people see at night.

mcq.q: What does a red traffic light tell a driver?
mcq.explanation: Red means stop.

mcq.q: What does a green traffic light tell a driver?
mcq.explanation: Green means go.

mcq.q: What do reflectors on a road or bicycle do?
options: Make their own light all night
Shine when car lights fall on them
mcq.explanation: Reflectors bounce light back.

mcq.q: How can lights help protect a home?
options: Security lights help keep thieves away
mcq.explanation: Thieves avoid places where they can be seen.

mcq.q: Why do some farmers use bright lights near animal pens at night?
mcq.explanation: Bright lights can scare away predators.

mcq.q: Which of these uses of light is for plants?
mcq.explanation: Plants use light to make food.

mcq.q: Which of these uses sunlight to dry things?
mcq.explanation: Sunlight dries wet things.

mcq.q: What do solar panels change sunlight into?
mcq.explanation: Solar panels make electricity from sunlight.

mcq.q: You want to see if a material is opaque. What do you do?
options: Shine a torch at it and see if light passes
mcq.explanation: If no light passes, it is opaque.

mcq.q: When light hits an opaque object, what forms behind it?
mcq.explanation: Blocked light makes a shadow.

mcq.q: Which of these is a safe practice with light?
options: Look at the sun with your eyes
Never look straight at the sun
mcq.explanation: Looking at the sun harms eyes.

mcq.q: Which of these is a torch used for?
options: To give light in the dark
mcq.explanation: A torch is an artificial light source.

mcq.q: Which of these is a benefit of good lighting when reading?
mcq.explanation: Enough light makes reading easier.

mcq.q: Which of these could you use to test three cards for straight line travel of light?
options: Cards with holes in the middle and a torch
mcq.explanation: Aligned holes let light pass only when straight.

mcq.q: Which of these is a way of making a room lighter during the day?
mcq.explanation: Open curtains let in more daylight.

mcq.q: Which of these is the biggest natural source of light for the Earth?
mcq.explanation: The sun lights the Earth in the daytime.

mcq.q: A lighthouse is used to
mcq.explanation: Lighthouses show ships where land or rocks are.

mcq.q: Which of these can be a cheap way of lighting a house in a rural area?
mcq.explanation: Solar lamps use free energy from the sun.

mcq.q: What is the purpose of skylights?
mcq.explanation: Skylights are roof openings or sheets that let light in.

mcq.q: Why is it better to use daylight than electric light in the day?
mcq.explanation: Sunlight is free.

mcq.q: Which of these makes its own light?
mcq.explanation: Glow-worms produce their own light.

mcq.q: Which of these only reflects light?
mcq.explanation: The moon reflects sunlight.

mcq.q: What is heat?
options: A form of energy that makes things hot
mcq.explanation: Heat is a form of energy.

mcq.q: Which instrument measures temperature?
mcq.explanation: A thermometer shows how hot something is.

mcq.q: In which unit is temperature measured in science?
mcq.explanation: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

mcq.q: At what temperature does water boil?
mcq.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

mcq.q: Which of these is the biggest natural source of heat for the Earth?
mcq.explanation: The sun heats the Earth.

mcq.q: Which of these is a source of heat from burning?
mcq.explanation: Charcoal gives out heat when it burns.

mcq.q: Which of these sources of heat uses electricity?
mcq.explanation: An electric iron uses electricity.

mcq.q: Which of these uses electricity to make heat?
mcq.explanation: A kettle is heated by electricity.

mcq.q: Which of these gives out heat when rubbed?
mcq.explanation: Rubbing produces heat through friction.
